origin: The 2025 declines, the southern loss of almost a third, the sixth mass bleaching, the 2026 regional bleaching event, Cyclone Narelle and the floods are accurate and on the fact sheet. "Coral cover is now at record lows" is contradicted by the fact sheet: AIMS put cover near the long-term average in each region and above it in the Northern and Central regions. "Collapsing" and "falling again in every region" are forecasts the fact sheet neither confirms nor rules out: 2026 brought new stressors, but the snapshot and AMCS both say the summer's bleaching was regional rather than mass. Expected honest rating: 30 to 50.

evidence_down.evidence_note: Real. AIMS, Annual Summary Report of Coral Reef Condition 2025/26, https://www.aims.gov.au/monitoring-great-barrier-reef/gbr-condition-summary-2025-26 (verified from Wayback snapshot 20260815042724). Verbatim: "Data were collected during manta tow surveys on 121 reefs ... between August 2025 and June 2026"; "In 2026, hard coral cover across all three regions of the GBR increased slightly or remained similar to levels recorded in 2025, signalling the start of recovery from the impacts of the 2024 mass bleaching event."; Northern "increased from 30.0% ... in 2025 to 35.1% ... coral cover remains above the long-term average of 27.0%"; Central "increased from 28.6% ... to 31.6% ... the estimate remains within the margin of error, with 2026 hard coral cover above the long-term average of 20.0%"; Southern "decreased slightly to 26.4% ... from 26.9% ... within the margin of error, and regional coral cover remains below the long-term average of 29.3%"; "Most surveys in the Northern GBR were completed before Cyclone Narelle passed through the region, limiting our ability to assess its impacts ... A more comprehensive assessment of Cyclone Narelle's impacts will be possible following surveys in 2027." Release date 11 August 2026: National Tribune reposting the Reef Authority's release ("released today (Tuesday, 11 August)"); ABC News, 2026-08-11; AIMS media release via EurekAlert; The Conversation, Daniela Ceccarelli (AIMS), published 2026-08-10 20:11 UTC.
pushes: New information that adds to the fact sheet: on August 11, 2026, AIMS released its annual summary for the 2025-26 survey season, covering 121 reefs surveyed between August 2025 and June 2026. Hard coral cover rose in the Northern region from 30.0% to 35.1% and in the Central region from 28.6% to 31.6% (AIMS said the central estimate is within the margin of error), and fell slightly in the Southern region from 26.9% to 26.4%, also within the margin of error. AIMS said the results signal 'the start of recovery from the impacts of the 2024 mass bleaching event'; Northern and Central cover are above their long-term averages and Southern cover remains below its long-term average of 29.3%. Most Northern surveys were completed before Cyclone Narelle, so AIMS will assess its impact in 2027 surveys. Does that change your rating?
Makes sense. What is your final number?
